{{Top|ffa}} {{Character |type=Galactic Empire |image=[[File:Jar_Jar_SWSB.png]] |name=Jar Jar Binks |homeworld=[[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]''[[The New Essential Guide to Characters]]'' |birth=[[52 BBY/Legends|52 BBY]],[[Star Wars: Episode I Insider's Guide|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Insider's Guide'']] states that Jar Jar Binks is twenty during the events of {{Film|I}}, which are dated to [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]] by ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''. Binks therefore must have been [[Reproduction/Legends|born]] in [[52 BBY/Legends|52 BBY]]. [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]{{Film|I}} |death= |species=[[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] {{C|[[Otolla/Legends|Otolla]]}} |gender=[[Gender/Legends|Male]] |pronouns=He/him |height=1.96 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] |mass=66 [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]]''[[Star Wars: Head-to-Head Tag Teams]]'' |hair= |feathers= |eyes=[[Color/Legends|Orange]] |skin= |cyber= |families=new |parents=*A [[Jar Jar Binks's father|father]] *A [[Jar Jar Binks's mother|mother]] |partners=new |siblings=new |children=new |affiliation=*[[Gungan society]] **[[Gungan High Council/Legends|Gungan High Council]]{{FactFile|54|JAR 9-10|Jar Jar Binks}} *[[Royal House of Naboo/Legends|Royal House of Naboo]]{{Film|II}} *[[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] **[[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]] *[[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]''[[Evasive Action: Prey]]'' **[[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]] |masters= |apprentices= }} {{Quote|Mesa clumsy.|Jar Jar Binks|}} '''Jar Jar Binks''' was the first [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] to represent his people in the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Galactic Senate]], first serving as a [[Junior Representative/Legends|Junior Representative]] along with Senator [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], and then, after her death, serving as full Senator himself. Like most Gungans, Binks was lanky and spoke [[Gungan (language)|Basic with a unique accent]]. Being naïve and clumsy, Jar Jar Binks contributed greatly to [[Galactic Empire/Legends|the fall]] of the [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]]. He was a [[General/Legends|General]], [[Junior Representative/Legends|Representative]], and later a [[Senator/Legends|Senator]]. Binks was also one of [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn's]] companions during the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]], traveling to distant worlds such as [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] and [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], an activity not taken up by many Gungans. On his return to Naboo, he served as a [[Bombad General/Legends|Bombad General]] for a short while in the [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]], and was a joint commander of the [[Battle of Naboo/Legends|Battle of the Great Grass Plains]] with General [[Tobler Ceel/Legends|Ceel]]. Binks later helped his people colonize the nearby Naboo moon [[Ohma-D'un/Legends|Ohma-D'un]]. During his career as Junior Representative, he acted as Amidala's proxy and proposed giving [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|Supreme Chancellor]] [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] emergency powers in order to deal with the [[Separatist Crisis/Legends|Separatist Crisis]]. Binks would continue his public service even after the death of Amidala, taking her place as Senator of the [[Chommell sector/Legends|Chommell sector]] in the newly-reformed [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]]. ==Biography== ===Early life=== Jar Jar Binks was born on the [[Mid Rim Territories]] [[planet]]''[[The Essential Atlas]]'' [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] in [[52 BBY/Legends|52 BBY]]. He grew up at [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]]. He had never become familiar with the orbits of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]’s moon or the planet’s rotation around the sun, as these were things he couldn’t see from the transport tubes of the city. {{Talesstart}} [[File:Young_Jar_Jar.jpg|thumb|left|270x270px|A young Binks with his father]] The son of [[Jar Jar Binks's father|George R. Binks]] and his [[Jar Jar Binks's mother|wife]] in [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]], Jar Jar Binks, was raised in his family traditions to be a great whaler as his ancestors had been for hundreds of years. Due to his clumsiness and ineptitude, however, Binks was never able to become what his father had wanted him to be. Once, while on an expedition to hunt a [[Naboo whale|whale]] in the southernmost seas of [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]], George ordered his son to hold the wheel steady; Binks, however, let go. This caused their ship to crash into the whale which resulted in the ship sinking to the bottom of the ocean.{{Tales|20|George R. Binks}} A month later, George Binks, his wife, and Jar Jar were all stranded on a [[Binks's Woe|desert island]]. When Binks offered to swim for help—a task which would have taken fifty years if it was possible at all—George Binks first called him a fool, telling him that he would be eaten within a day, but then realized this would result in Jar Jar Binks death and told him that it was a good idea. Binks was about to jump into the water when George's wife reprimanded him and stopped George from allowing him to do so. Unable to take it anymore George lamented over what could have been; he called his son an imbecile and attempted to commit suicide by shooting himself with his [[Blaster pistol/Legends|blaster pistol]] but only grazed his head, resulting in it not being lethal. Binks later found his way back to Otoh Gunga. {{Talesend}} ===Life in Otoh Gunga=== ==== Meeting Tarpals ==== [[File:Otoh Gunga on locap.png|thumb|270x270px|[[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]], the city where Jar Jar Binks lived during much of his early life.]] Banished in all of [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga's]] schools and not able to turn to his parents for guidance, Binks hopped between job after job throughout his youth. His clumsiness inevitably got him fired before sunset. Once, Binks was working as a street-side [[shudderup]] musician when a passerby paid him money to stop the music. That is when he was discovered by local lawbreaker [[Roos Tarpals/Legends|Roos Tarpals]], the leader of a small band of young thieves. Binks was given the job of distracting security patrols while Tarpals and his gang pulled off various scams. Unlike the other thieves, Tarpals treated Binks like a valued team member and a friend. This friendship ended when Tarpals enlisted in the [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]]. The band soon scattered and Binks again began searching for his place in life. Fortunately, Boss [[Rugor Nass/Legends|Rugor Nass]], ruler of Otoh Gunga, arranged new employment for Binks, partly out of respect for [[Jar Jar Binks's father|his]] [[Jar Jar Binks's mother|parents]], and partly on the request of now-Captain Tarpals. Jar Jar's clumsiness resulted in unfortunate incidents with the city sewer system. Whenever an accident occurred there, everyone immediately assumed Jar Jar was responsible - and they were usually right. ==== Rescue in the Core ==== [[File:Gungan High Council.png|left|thumb|270x270px|Boss [[Rugor Nass/Legends|Nass]] and the [[Gungan High Council/Legends|Gungan Council]] (pictured) had to decide Jar Jar's place in the society.]] After a petition signed by over three hundred citizens to remove Jar Jar Binks to a far-off bubble was torn up by Nass, and the [[Gungan High Council/Legends|Rep Council]]’s suggestion of removing Jar Jar to a military post on the surface was also dismissed by the Boss, Jar Jar Binks was given a job as a bubble cleaner for the [[Otoh Gunga Zoological Research Facility]] to keep him out of trouble. While cleaning the [[Hrumph/Legends|hrumph]] cage, Jar Jar accidentally let one loose and chased after it, not realizing that in doing so, he was letting the others escape as well. They are all eventually rounded up, but by then, they have made it to the control room and accidentally freed the [[Great Hohokum]] and two [[Dwarf opee sea killer|dwarf opee sea killers]] from their bubbles. The Director of the Zoological Research Facility found Jar Jar asleep after chasing one [[Hrumph/Legends|hrumph]] and took him to Boss Nass. Jar Jar was not going to be pounded,''[[Episode I Adventures 9: Rescue in the Core]]'' but Nass sentenced him to six months of hard labor in the [[Quarry penal colony]], where prisoners were sentenced to shape and reshape boulders generations before. The quarry had been shut down for a long time, but it was set to be reopen just for Jar Jar.[[File:Bongo.jpg|thumb|270x270px|Jar Jar Binks had to travel on a Bongo (pictured) for his upcoming punishment.]] Upon reaching the docking platform to take Jar Jar to the quarry, Nass discovers that the military bongo was out chasing down escaped animals, and Rep [[Teers/Legends|Teers]] had already left in the Rep heyblibber, so they had to take a [[Tribubble bongo/Legends|tribubble bongo]], which meant that only Jar Jar, Nass, and Commander [[Wollod (Gungan)|Wollod]] could go. They headed for the quarry, but on the way, they learnt that a seaquake has endangered Teers’ heyblibber and the lives of Teers and the pilot, Major [[Fassa (Gungan)|Fassa]]. They prepared to go on a rescue mission, but a shockwave hit the bongo and knocked all but Jar Jar out. He managed to get them into the safety of the quarry, but they were trapped inside by a cave-in. Jar Jar made sure the other two were okay, then set out to find a way to leave the quarry. He found an albino [[Dianoga/Legends|dianoga]] from the research facility that had hitched a ride on the bongo. Jar Jar knocked it out and prepared to take it back with them. After battling [[Veermok/Legends|veermoks]] and sea creatures, Jar Jar made it to the control room and started to fill the room with the bongo with water to raise them to an escape tunnel. As Jar Jar raced back to the bongo, he found the two dwarf opees and made them come with him. Finally, Jar Jar got the bongo and the opees out of the area and to where they help save the heyblibber from another creature before finally arriving at a bubble in [[Lake Umberbool]]. Teers, Nass, Wollod, and Fassa are found, but Captain Tarpals still took Jar Jar into custody, until Nass asked to see him. Nass thanked him for saving their lives, and allowed Jar Jar to remain on Otoh Gunga on probation and to watch the upcoming [[Festival of Warriors]]. Nass then introduced Jar Jar to Fassa, actually his niece, who happened to believe she owed Jar Jar a life debt for saving her and Teers. Fassa asked if Jar Jar would be competing in the festival, and he could only gulp and know that since she has asked, he would have to compete. ==== Festival of the Warriors ==== While Jar Jar Binks was assigned to prepare for the [[Festival of Warriors]], Major Fassa’s pursuit of him caused him to lie and say Boss Nass wanted him to work in the kitchen. This brings Nass fuming after Jar Jar, but he soon learnt why Jar Jar had lied and forgives him the error. To prove that he was not just a clumsy foul-up, Jar Jar entered into the [[Big Nasty Free-For-All|Big Nasty Free-for-All]] among 436 contestants, which Fassa had expected him to do. Jar Jar arrived thirteenth in the challenge.[[Episode I Adventures 10: Festival of Warriors|''Episode I Adventures 10: Festival of Warriors'']] He was later called to witness alongside Boss Nass, Tarpals, Fassa, and engineer [[Lob Dizz]], to look over droids that were captured by Fassa during the Big Nasty Free-For-All. When the droids didn't want to give up information about their mission, the Gungans had a couple of the out of commission droids turned into garbage disposals, using Jar Jar’s voice through a megaphone to scare the droids. The droids weren't necessarily scared, but they sure didn't want to end up talking like the Gungans, so they told them about [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Pirate/Legends|pirate]] [[Swagg]]’s plans, and that he still has ten droids. Along with Commander [[Wollod (Gungan)|Wollod]], the group of Gungans raced to stop Swagg. They send Jar Jar (thinking he’ll get killed, though Fassa didn't like that one bit) to Rep [[Been]]’s captured sub to find and rescue him. Through sheer dumb luck, Jar Jar actually succeeded in getting aboard and defeating some droids, but Been was not aboard. The Gungans raced through the jungle to stop Swagg and the droids, and along the way, Jar Jar got caught in a trap. Tarpals found him, but decided not to free him yet, so that he couldn't cause any more trouble. Swagg eventually fled in an escape pod, while Tarpals piloted the ship back to [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. After talking to the others, Tarpals realized he still had to get Jar Jar down, so he raced for the trap. Jar Jar was cut down, but he was dizzy from blood rushing to his head. Playing off of Tarpals’ guilt, Jar Jar got permission to attend the upcoming [[Bongo Rally]].[[Episode I Adventures 11: Pirates from Beyond the Sea|''Episode I Adventures 11: Pirates from Beyond the Sea'']] Boss Nass was not amused that Major Fassa had taken a life debt to Jar Jar Binks, but luckily he discovered from Rep [[Been]] that since Jar Jar was on probation, the life debt was invalid. As Jar Jar returned to [[Lake Umberbool]] for work, two bongo racers, [[Spleed Nukkels]] and [[Neb Neb Goodrow]], got into an accident during prerace trials. Jar Jar, having been given his Bongo Rally tickets but being talked into working at Boss Nass’ party in Otoh Gunga, went with the two racers back to [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]], where the racers intended to get other bongos. Upon arrival, they found [[Lob Dizz]] knocked out and explosions threatening the lab. Dizz and Neb Neb went to fix the city’s communications array to warn those in Lake Umberbool of [[Swagg]]’s return, while Jar Jar and Nukkels chased down the pirate, who had stolen a ferry. They arrived at Umberbool and Jar Jar managed to take out one of the pirate's two droids. Swagg and the other droid escaped as Nukkels twisted her ankle. Jar Jar continued after the intruders, discovering that one of them has taken the place of racer Brooboo Seep. Jar Jar quickly warned Tarpals and Fassa and escaped before Nass could see that he wasn't not at Otoh Gunga. Later Tarpals saved Jar Jar’s hide by not saying how he knew Swagg was coming.[[Episode I Adventures 12: The Bongo Rally|''Episode I Adventures 12: The Bongo Rally'']] ==== Final banishment ==== {{Quote|You were banished because you were clumsy?|Obi-Wan Kenobi|}} [[File:Jar_Jar_banished.png|thumb|270x270px|Boss Rugor Nass banishes Jar Jar Binks.]] Later, Boss Nass threw a lavish party at his mansion and gave Binks a job in the kitchen as a waiter.[[Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary|''Star Wars: Episode I: The Visual Dictionary'']] However, Binks destroyed the gasser oven. The explosion cracked the bubble wall and flooded the party. Binks tried to save Boss Nass's luxury [[Heyblibber/Legends|heyblibber]], but ended up crashing it instead and flooding several adjoining bubble. The final straw was a disastrous display before Boss Nass, who was outraged, and decided that he had had enough. As this was not Jar Jars first serious accident or even his first serious flooding accident, a furious Boss Nass and the rest of the [[Gungan High Council/Legends|Gungan High Council]] [[High Board Room/Legends|Chamber of Judgment]] invoked the [[Nocombackie law/Legends|Nocombackie Law]], banishing Binks and preventing him from ever returning to Otoh Gunga upon pain of death. Jar Jar was brougth to a swampy bank and watched Captain Tarpals wade back through the water to the waiting bongo. Jar Jar felt a pain in his stomach as he realized he might never see a bongo or any Gungan again. He watched Tarpals climb into the bongo, and wasn’t surprised when Tarpals didn’t wave goodbye. He kept his eyes on the vessel until it sank below the water’s surface. The bongo left a small trail of bubbles, and he couldn’t help but watch them, too, until each one of them had surfaced and the water was completely still. As he was left alone, he hoped that he would be allowed to go home again [[File:Tarpals intervention.png|left|thumb|250x250px|Tarpals intervines to save Jar Jar (and bringing him to his banishment).]] Jar Jar Binks hide back in Otoh Gunga but [[Captain/Legends|Captain]] Tarpals found him in Chef [[Brass Marshoo]]'s restaurant scrounging for scraps. Tarpals apprehended him and prepared to take him to the surface, however, he was ambushed by Marshoo and several thugs. Tarpals was knocked out in the scuffle, but Binks saved him, also thanks with the help of Tarpals' [[Kaadu/Legends|kaadu]]. The hapless Gungan pleaded with Tarpals for clemency, but was ignored. Tarpals then escorted Binks to the shores of the [[Lianorm Swamp/Legends|Lianorm Swamp]], the place of Binks's banishment.{{Tales|3|The Death of Captain Tarpals}} It was not the easiest of tasks since, despite their differences, Tarpals and Binks were friends, albeit mismatched ones.{{DB|character|captaintarpals|Tarpals, Captain}} The orphaned Binks{{DB|character|jarjarbinks|Binks, Jar Jar}} was forced to live in the [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] [[Forest/Legends|forests]], now his adopted homelands[[Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I|''Inside the Worlds of Star Wars: Episode I'']] in a luckless exile. He survived on his own, eating raw [[Shellfish/Legends|shellfish]] and other such swamp fare. His long muscular tongue helped him to scoop molluscs out of their shells and tasty [[Gumbol/Legends|gumbols]] out of their [[Tree/Legends|tree]] burrows. Like most [[Gungan/Legends|Gungans]], he preferred to catch his food fresh.[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (junior novelization)|''Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace'' junior novelization]] [[Roos Tarpals/Legends|Tarpals]] kept an eye on the bumbling outcast, making sure the youngster didn't re-enter Gungan society. The long months spent in exile were among the worst of Jar Jar's life. ===Blockade of Naboo=== ====Meeting the Jedi==== {{Quote|I spake.''"
"''The ability to speak does not make you intelligent. Now get out of here.|Jar Jar and Qui-Gon Jinn|}} [[File:QGJSavesJJB-SWE.png|thumb|left|270x270px|Qui-Gon Jinn saves Binks's life.]] One day in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]],''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' places the [[Invasion of Naboo/Legends|Invasion of Naboo]] in [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]]. Binks went out foraging for food in the [[Lianorm Swamp/Legends|Lianorm Swamp]] as the early morning mist was just beginning to thin. He found a shell by the side of a pool[[The Phantom Menace (Mighty Chronicles)|''The Phantom Menace (''Mighty Chronicles)]] that he pried open, with its long tongue licking out the insides with a quick whipping movement[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (novelization)|''Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace'' novelization]] and enjoying its delicate flavor and smoothness. Unfortunately his hunting was interrupted[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (book-and-record)|''Star Wars:'' Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' (book-and-record)]] when he stumbled across [[OOM-9/Legends|OOM-9's]] [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] invasion force. Startled by the noise, Binks jumped to his feet and cast aside the empty shell. Panicking, he bumped into [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]], an ambassador who had been sent to resolve the crisis between the Naboo and the Federation. Jinn tackled Binks to the ground and held him there to prevent them both from getting crushed by a [[Multi-Troop Transport/Legends|Multi-Troop Transport]] that was passing by. As a result of this life-saving act, Binks, despite being an outcast, adhered to the Gungan principle of a [[Life debt/Legends|life debt]] and insisted on following Jinn, much to the Jedi's annoyance. Both Jinn and his [[Padawan/Legends|apprentice]], [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], needed to contact Queen [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Amidala]] in Theed, but had no way of reaching her. Binks suggested that they go to Otoh Gunga, his old home, but quickly regretted mentioning it. The Jedi persuaded him to take them there, but Binks rightly feared for his life. Despite this, such faithful meeting would change the life of the naive Gungan.{{SW|url=news/meet-the-gungans-a-history-of-naboo-bombad-aliens|text=Meet the Gungans: A History of Naboo's Bombad Aliens|nolive=1}} [[File:Jar_Jar_meets_Jedi.png|thumb|270x270px|Binks meets Qui-Gon Jinn and Obi-Wan Kenobi.]]The two Jedi escorted Binks past twenty battle droids and a half-built droid camp. Binks panicked and ran off, leaving the Jedi to [[Force jump/Legends|Force Jump]] up mushrooms to reach the top of the tree and the nearby plateaus, which they traversed, eventually moving into a cave, where they faced a [[Slaatik hagworm]]. After defeating the hagworm, they then rejoined Binks and continued their journey.[[Star Wars: Episode I Jedi Power Battles|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''Jedi Power Battles'']] [[File:Otoh Gunga TPM.png|left|thumb|270x270px|Jar Jar and the Jedi arrive at [[Otoh Gunga/Legends|Otoh Gunga]].]] Jar Jar guided them to [[Lake Paonga/Legends|Lake Paonga]], where they had to swim underwater to reach the city. Despite the Jedi swam quickly, several times Jar Jar had to stop and wait for them to catch up. Upon reaching Otoh Gunga, Binks was arrested by his old friend, Tarpals, and brought before Nass, the former also telling Binks upon arresting him that he was in "big doo-doo thisa time." Jar Jar's arrival was reported by Tarpals to Nass, including that he had brought two Jedi with him.[[Gungan Trouble!|''Gungan Trouble!'']] [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] bartered with Nass, and persuaded him to provide them with transportation to Theed. Following that, Nass sentenced Binks to death, but Jinn quickly interceded, citing that Binks's life belonged to him, due to the Gungan life debt system. Nass had Binks freed and sent along with the Jedi to Theed. Binks was dismayed over the fact that he had to tag along with the Jedi, but he figured that he had a higher chance of survival with them than in Otoh Gunga. In turn Qui-Gon made the decision to bring Jar Jar Binks along not because he was a skilled navigator, but because he was another project that Qui-Gon had determined had value and could be reclaimed. During the undersea journey he paid по attention to submarine piloting ог to finding his way beyond his swamp home, and was petrified of deep-sea creatures lurking in the caverns, in a core that was more terrible that even he had imagined. [[File:Bisected-Droids.png|thumb|270x270px|Jar Jar sees [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]] cutting down droids with his [[Qui-Gon Jinn's lightsaber/Legends|ligthsaber]].]] Upon reaching Federation-occupied Theed, they had to abandon the bongo as the current was pulling them towards a waterfall. With the fuel gauge empty, Qui-Gon reached for his utility belt and closed his fingers around his grappling-spike launcher, wraping it around a railing. Once they had reached safety, they could make their way to Theed.[[Episode I Adventures 13: Danger on Naboo|''Episode I Adventures 13: Danger on Naboo'']] The central bridge across the river was blasted apart by an [[Armored Assault Tank/Legends|Armored Assault Tank]], cutting the city off from other regions and separating the group. Kenobi eventually met back up with Jinn and Binks.[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]] Binks watched as the Jedi [[Capture of Theed/Legends|rescued]] the Queen, and escorted her to safety. Jinn convinced the Queen to go to [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], to plead her case to the Senate, a choice that would result in Binks leaving the planet for the very first time. While the Queen's ship got past the Federation blockade of the planet, it sustained mild damage, and lost its hyperdrive capacity, leaving it only enough power to reach [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]], the only planet in the area devoid of Federation presence. Jar Jar Binks was left in the droid storage hold, where he couldn’t get into much trouble. The [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] didn't seem to have any orders regarding the Gungan, so they simply left him to his own devices. Every time he touched something, someone shouted at him to leave it alone. And when they didn’t shout, whatever he touched spat springs or sparks or bits of metal, and ''then'' they shouted. At the back of the cabinet, he picked an oilcan and bounded into the central area of the ship, where the Queen’s handmaiden was cleaning up [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]]. They three met and the Gugan helped her clean the droid. ====Beyond Naboo==== {{Quote|This sun doin' murder to mesa skin…|Jar Jar Binks|}} [[File:Gozanti cruiser-TPM.png|thumb|270x270px|Binks and his friends visiting [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]].]] Upon reaching Tatooine, Jinn, Binks, Amidala (disguised as a handmaiden), and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] ventured into the city of [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]] in search of new parts for the ship. As Mos Espa was a multinational spaceport, Jar Jar would had made Qui-Gon appear less obvious by going along. They came across [[Wald's Parts|Watto's Shop]], which had the parts they needed. However, they had no way of purchasing them, due to the [[Galactic Credit Standard/Legends|Republic Credit's]] lack of use in backwater planets like Tatooine. At Watto's Shop, they encountered a young boy, [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker]].[[File:Sebulba_bullying_Binks.png|thumb|left|270x270px|Binks being bullied by Sebulba]]Later, near a market, an hungry[[Jar Jar's Mistake|''Jar Jar's Mistake'']] Jar Jar attempted to eat a [[Gorg/Legends|Gorg]], as he had not eaten in some time. He was pulling in his mouth before learning from [[Gragra/Legends|Gragra]] that the Gorg cost seven [[Wupiupi/Legends|wupiupi]]. As his companions were already out of sight the Gungan spitted the animal away in desperation, landing it in the [[Soup/Legends|soup]] of [[Podracer/Legends|podracer]] [[Sebulba/Legends|Sebulba]], who threatened to beat Binks to a pulp. Only the timely intervention of Skywalker saved him. Skywalker was but a poor slave, nonetheless, he offered the group shelter and hospitality when they were caught in a sandstorm. At his home, they discovered that he had a talent for [[Podracing/Legends|podracing]], which Skywalker thought would be a good way for Jinn and Amidala to get the money required for the new hyperdrive. As they were allowed to stay for the nigth, Jar Jar Binks was curled up on the kitchen floor in a fetal position, snoring loudly. [[File:Jedi reflexes.png|thumb|270x270px|Binks is stopped from using is tounge by [[Qui-Gon Jinn/Legends|Qui-Gon Jinn]].]] Binks was more than willing to help in the enterprise, offering to perform maintenance on Skywalker's podracer. Whether or not his efforts were of any help was irrelevant: he once got his hand stuck in one of the compressors of the engines of Skywalker's podracer, as well as inadvertently causing his tongue to go numb from making contact with the energy binders while getting up to retrieve a wrench he dropped. Anakin was vaguely aware of Jar Jar’s garbled voice,[[Episode I Adventures 14: Podrace to Freedom|''Episode I Adventures 14: Podrace to Freedom'']] but still appreciated the assistance. On the day of the [[Boonta Eve Classic/Legends|Boonta Eve Classic]] Race, Jar Jar Binks spotted a [[Trooshti/Legends|trooshti]] stealing a battery charger from [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Anakin Skywalker's]] [[Anakin Skywalker's Podracer/Legends|podracer]] and pursued the insect, gaining [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]]'s reluctant help. Jar Jar managed to capture the thief with his extendable tongue, but it passed the charging unit to another trooshti. The two commandeered a [[Speeder/Legends|speeder]] to chase the insect into the Tatooine desert and escaped two angry [[Gamorrean|Gamorreans]] that Jar Jar had clumsily run into. While in pursuit, Jar Jar threatened the captured insect, however Padmé stopped him, arguing that civilized beings needn't resort to violence. The chase lead them to an abandoned [[Moisture farm/Legends|moisture farm]] where the trooshti colony had used an underground pump to create a small oasis of [[Water/Legends|water]]. There they learned that the pump was malfunctioning and the colony appeared to be using the charger to attempt to re-prime it. Padmé offered to help repair the pump if the colony would return the charger and also protect her from the Gamorreans, who had just arrived on the scene. While the trooshti swarmed the Gamorreans, Padmé worked on the pump and got it working just as the warriors slipped into the water, surprised by Jar Jar resurfacing in the water. There, they were attacked by [[Peppi Bow/Legends|Peppi Bow]], a female Gungan. She explained that there was something wrong with the water. They followed the stream and found a secret lab. Amidala asked for reinforcements, but they were quickly captured by Dr. [[Nuvo Vindi/Legends|Nuvo Vindi]], who had been creating an airborne sample of the deadly [[Blue Shadow Virus/Legends|Blue Shadow Virus]], and his droids. Soon after, however, they were saved by Skywalker and the clones. Kenobi and Tano arrived soon after for impeding anyone release the virus. The doctor had created a set of bombs containing the virus, and if they exploded, the whole planet would be infected. Fortunately, the clones were able to deactivate them while Skywalker and Kenobi searched for Vindi. They found out that one of the bombs was missing but Binks found the droid that had stolen it and saved all of the people from Naboo. Amidala soon found out that one of the tubes with the virus was missing. The entire lab was covered with the virus and Tano and the clones were contaminated. Binks and Amidala, who were wearing protective suits, helped to destroy the rest of the droids, preventing the virus's escape. In an attempt to help, Binks wanted to shoot one of the droids but hit Amidala suit, thus contaminating Amidala as well. Luckily, Skywalker and Kenobi returned with a cure for the virus. While the contaminated were being removed, Kenobi told Binks that he had been very brave fending off the battle droids and that they might have him trained with a blaster. Binks was very excited.{{TCW|Mystery of a Thousand Moons}} ==== The Frozen Planet ==== [[File:Skirmish on Hoth.jpg|thumb|316x316px|Jar Jar Binks and Obi Wan on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]].]] Jar Jar Binks and [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], along with some clone troopers, participated to a diplomatic event where Obi-Wan was Jar Jar’s guard. On their way back to Coruscant, they were attacked by droid starfighters and crashed on [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]. When caught between battle droids on one side and [[Wampa/Legends|wampas]] on the other, they set the two against each other, then escaped in a Separatist landing ship.{{TCWComicCite|6.34|Frozen Out!}} ====War on Dac==== Following the assassination of the [[Mon Calamari/Legends|Mon Calamari]] [[King/Legends|King]] [[Yos Kolina/Legends|Yos Kolina]], tensions broke out between the Mon Calamari and [[Quarren]] on the planet [[Dac/Legends|Dac]]. The Quarrens regarded Kolina's successor, Prince [[Lee-Char]], as too inexperienced to rule. The Separatist Ambassador [[Riff Tamson/Legends|Riff Tamson]], stirred up trouble between the Mon Calamari and Quarren. In response, the Republic sent Senator Amidala and the two Jedi Skywalker and Kit Fisto to mediate between the two parties. With Separatist backing, the Quarren overthrew the Dac government and waged war against the Mon Calamari and their Republic allies.{{TCW|Water War}} In response to the outbreak of [[Battle of Mon Cala/Legends|fighting]] on Mon Cala, the Republic sent Obi-Wan Kenobi to seek the help of Gungan reinforcements since the Gungans were an amphibious species. Binks successfully convinced the [[Gungan High Council/Legends|Gungan High Council]] to send the [[Gungan Grand Army/Legends|Gungan Grand Army]] to relieve Mon Cala. Binks and the Gungan reinforcements arrived just in time to render valuable aid to Skywalker, Amidala, and Lee Char. However, the Separatist Commander Tamson counter-attacked by using his [[Trident-class assault ship/Legends|''Trident''-class assault ships]] to create artificial whirlpools which disoriented the Gungan forces. During the fighting, Binks and the Gungan reinforcements were captured by Tamson's Separatist forces.{{TCW|Gungan Attack}} Following their defeat, Representative Binks along with Skywalker, Amidala, and Kit Fisto were brought before Commander Tamson, who interrogated them about the whereabouts of Prince Lee Char. During the interrogation, Tamson cracked Amidala's faceplate but Binks was able to seal it with slime generated by his Gungan physiology. Meanwhile, Prince Lee Char and Anakin's Padawan Ahsoka succeeded in freeing the Mon Calamari prisoners and convincing the Mon Calamari and Quarrens to work together to drive out the Separatist invaders. During the ensuing battle, Binks and the other prisoners were rescued while Tamson was killed by Lee Char. Following the end of the fighting, Lee Char was recognized as the new King of Mon Cala by both the Mon Calamari and Quarren species.{{TCW|Prisoners}} ====Conflict on Naboo==== [[File:NeeyutneeLeaves-SW.png|thumb|270x270px|Jar Jar Binks after resolving the [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] crisis.]] Later, there was a crisis on Naboo. Boss [[Lyonie/Legends|Lyonie]] was calling for the Gungan Grand Army to invade Theed. He was secretly under the sway of Separatist-allied minister [[Rish Loo/Legends|Rish Loo]]. Binks summoned Skywalker and Amidala to meet with him, and brought them before Lyonie. Skywalker realized Lyonie was mind-controlled by a necklace, and [[Telekinesis/Legends#Force pull|Force-yanked]] it off. Lyonie then confronted Loo and was stabbed, while Loo ran from Otoh Gunga and tried to rally the army with news of Lyonie's demise.{{TCW|Shadow Warrior}} Amidala noticed Binks bore a resemblance to Boss Lyonie and had him assume his identity. "Lyonie" was able to call off the Grand Army, but General [[Grievous/Legends|Grievous]] arrived. Binks continued his masquerade to buy time for General Tarpals to sabotage Grievous' droid guards. Binks fled from Grievous' ship in time to view the duel between two Generals. Tarpals sacrificed himself to defeat the Separatist leader. Binks was later present when the Gungans traded General Grievous for Skywalker, who had been captured by Count Dooku. Queen [[Neeyutnee/Legends|Neeyutnee]] then thanked Binks for resolving another crisis between Naboo's two species, as he had done years earlier. ====Mission to Bardotta==== [[File:EpGuide609.png|thumb|270x270px|Jar Jar Binks and Mace Windu on Bardotta|left]] Following the near civil war on Naboo, Representative Jar Jar Binks was called upon by the Galactic Republic to deal with a new crisis on the planet [[Bardotta/Legends|Bardotta]]. Several [[Dagoyan Masters/Legends|Dagoyan Masters]] had mysteriously disappeared. There was a prophecy that if the Masters were not returned, a great darkness would descend on the planet. Distrusting the Jedi Order for inducting [[Bardottan]] children, [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Julia/Legends|Julia]] had requested a special meeting with Binks to discuss the crisis. Despite the Queen's request that Binks travel to Bardotta alone, the [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Mace Windu/Legends|Mace Windu]] suspected something was afoot and accompanied Binks by posing as his servant.{{TCW|The Disappeared, Part I}} Binks met with the Queen but she was kidnapped during the meeting. In response, the remaining Dagoyan Masters convened the [[Bahk-tov Council/Legends|Bahk-tov Council]], where [[High Seneschal/Legends|High Seneschal]] [[Peteen/Legends|Peteen]] informed them of a prophecy that if the queen was not found within three rotations, she would be gone forever and an era of darkness would descend on the galaxy. Binks and Windu also learnt from another Council member named [[Savatte/Legends|Savatte]] that the prophecy originated from the malevolent [[Frangawl Cult/Legends|Frangawl Cult]], whose shrine to the demon [[Malmourral/Legends|Malmourral]] was underneath the Dagoyan temple. While exploring the catacombs below the temple, Binks was captured by a Frangawl cultist, who blew a glowing powder into his face which temporarily made him invisible. The cult members placed Binks in a cage suspended above a lava pit where he found the other captured Dagoyan masters, who informed him that they were to be sacrificed to Malmourral. Binks managed to contact Master Windu with his [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] and transmit his location. However, the [[Frangawl cult leader/Legends|Frangawl cult leader]] discovered it and had it destroyed. Binks also encountered Julia who revealed that the Frangawl cultists were stealing the Force from the Dagoyan masters. The Frangawl cultists then attempted to sacrifice Binks himself. However, Master Windu arrived and managed to fight off the cult members and free Binks. Unfortunately, the cult leader escaped the planet with the Queen in a starship. In response, Binks vowed to rescue Queen Julia with the help of Master Windu. While traveling through space, Binks recounted to Master Windu how he had witnessed the cultists sacrificing one of the Dagoyan Masters and extracting the [[Living Force/Legends|Living Force]] from his body which they stored in the [[Bardottan Sphere/Legends|Bardottan Sphere]]. Based on this information, Windu deduced that the cultists would extract the Living Force from Queen Julia herself and used his Force powers to track her location. Their travels took them to a market square on the moon [[Zardossa Stix/Legends|Zardossa Stix]]. Amidst the crowd, Binks caught up with the screaming Julia but found himself cornered by several of the cultists. Binks managed to flee his pursuers and tried to pursue the group with the captive Queen. During the ensuing chaos, Windu saved Binks from being gunned down by a cultist armed with a [[EWHB-12 heavy repeating blaster]].{{TCW|The Disappeared, Part II}} Continuing their pursuit, Binks and Windu were set upon by an animal trainer and his two [[Gundark/Legends|gundarks]]. During the fray, the trainer relieved Windu of his lightsaber using his whip. Binks then punched the trainer and retrieved the lightsaber with his tongue, and returned it to the Jedi Master. Windu managed to stun one of the gundarks and to kill the other. Binks continued the pursuit but the cultists escaped in two speeders. After questioning the trainer, Binks and Windu continued their rescue mission on an [[Eopie/Legends|eopie]] and [[Dalgo/Legends|dalgo]]. Meanwhile, the cultists arrived at a Zardossan temple where they were joined by the [[Nightsisters/Legends|Nightsister]] [[Mother (title)/Legends|Mother]] [[Talzin/Legends|Talzin]] who wanted to sacrifice Queen Julia in order to steal her Force energy. After tangling with the temple's [[Stone guardian/Legends|Stone guardians]], Windu and Binks stormed the temple. While Windu and Mother Talzin fought, Binks used one of the stone guardian's weapons to blast the cult members and to free Queen Julia from her bonds. While Binks grappled with the cult leader, the planets aligned and a beam of energy blasted through a series of lenses. While the cult leader was killed by the blast of energy, Julia managed to push Binks out of harm's way. The Force sphere fell from its pedestal and shattered, releasing a powerful explosion. Binks along with Windu and Julia managed to survive this explosion and escape the temple. Following her rescue, Queen Julia thanked Binks and Windu and expressed hope that these events would lead to better understanding between the Bardottans and the Jedi. ===Galactic Empire=== {{Quote|It is such a tragedy. The Gungans are so peaceful, so cute and kind. Well, Jar Jar—I met him once. He's a bit annoying.|Vaik'anna Silverlight during the time of the Galactic Civil War|{{GalaxiesAED}}}} [[File:MourningforPadme.jpg|thumb|270x270px|Binks at the funeral of Padmé Amidala]] Jar Jar Binks continued to represent the Gungans in Naboo's senatorial delegation throughout the Clone Wars, though his accomplishments in politics were never as significant as his vote on the Military Creation Act. He had also apparently learned to keep his mouth shut after the "Emergency Powers" debacle, learning from his substantial mistake that had led to one of the bloodiest wars in galactic history. Jar Jar Binks was present at the [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]] when Palpatine presented the Jedi treachery and founded the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]]. He returned to Naboo and after the death of his friend and colleague [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]], he was one of the chief mourners at her funeral on Naboo along with Boss Nass,{{Film|III}} and succeeded her Senatorial position, representing the [[Chommell sector/Legends|Chommell sector]] in the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]] beginning in [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]].{{Hyperspace|url=hyperspace/source/writtenword/index.html?page=1|text=The Written Word|int=The Written Word}} After the formation of the [[New Order/Legends|New Order]], Binks was considered an ally of the new Emperor, and an [[Imperial HoloVision]] report shortly after the end of the Clone Wars mentioned that he had personally sent Senator Binks to an undisclosed location. === Later life === Jar Jar was succeeded in his post as Representative of Naboo at the Galactic Senate by [[Pooja Naberrie/Legends|Pooja Naberrie]], one of [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]]'s nieces. He retired to a quiet life and, after more adventures around the galaxy that any [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] ever hoped for, he was happy to fade into obscurity.{{FactFile2014|55|JAR 11-16|Jar Jar Binks}} During the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], following the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]] in [[0 BBY/Legends|0 BBY]], a [[Twi'lek/Legends|Twi'lek]] by the name of [[Vaik'anna Silverlight]] remarked to a spacer in Theed that she had met Jar Jar, and found him to be a bit annoying. Binks was alive and well in [[7 ABY/Legends|6.5 ABY]], and was present on Coruscant during its [[Liberation of Coruscant (Galactic Civil War)|liberation]] from the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] by troops of the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. While he was never involved in this liberation, he was situated relatively close to some of the action.''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]'' ==Personality and traits== {{Quote|The ship has been destroyed.''"
"''Battle droids?''"
"''No.''"
"''Jar Jar?''"
"''Jar Jar.|[[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Padmé Amidala]] after Binks accidentally destroys her [[H-type Nubian yacht/Legends|starship]]|audio=ShipHasBeenDestroyed-BJ.flac|}} [[File:JarJar-PhotoMasher.png|thumb|right|250px|Binks demonstrating his clumsiness]] Jar Jar Binks was clumsier than most of his fellow Gungans, which was the reason why he was banished from Otoh Gunga. He would often explain his dislike, lashing out with his long tongue. Like all Gungans, he spoke with a pidgin Gungan dialect of [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Galactic Basic]], which sometimes made him hard to understand. Despite his clumsiness, Binks used to be a keen dancer, and he was known to perform notably [[Deesco]]''[[Star Wars: Early Learning Activity Center]]'' and the [[Gungan Style]].[[Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures (video game)|''Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures'']] Jar Jar Binks struggled to prove his worth throughout his life. He often held a certain irreverence for his superiors—often making faces behind their backs, but he would still obey their orders. He was socially active, trying to communicate with sentients around him, and making new friends. He had some aptitude mechanically; he was able to perform maintenance on Anakin Skywalker's pod. As a diplomat, he helped unite the Gungans and the Naboo in 32 BBY. For that deed, he was promoted to general. He would lead the Gungan army against the battle droids, destroying many of them, even if sometimes by accident. In other adventures during the course of the Clone Wars, Binks displayed hidden talents of intellect and improvisation despite his clumsiness and nervousness, contributing greatly to Republic victories on either diplomatic or special combat missions. As a politician, Binks successfully represented the Gungans for several years, but when he had to take the role of senator, he was easily manipulated by Palpatine's cronies. The [[Naboo (people)/Legends|Naboo]] elevated a simple, well-meaning soul to a position that may had been beyond his abilities. While his compassion spoke volumes of the quality of his character, his inherent gullibility and trusting nature were easily exploited by the less scrupulous in the field of politics. For many, Jar Jar was but a joke, the subject of derision, but in the corrupt inner confines of [[Galactic Senate/Legends|Senate]], his lanky frame stood as a rare example of non-corrupt politician interested only in the greater good of the Republic and his people. His dedication to his friends made him a very reliable associate and ally, whether it be on a diplomatic or combat mission. He had a great empathy for all beings and was in some ways a true innocent.[[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|''Star Wars:'' Episode I ''The Phantom Menace: Prima's Official Strategy Guide'']] When hungry, Jar Jar ate nearly anything without a second thought, a habit eared from being exiled the [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]] swamps. ==Behind the scenes== {{Quote|There is a group of fans for the films that doesn't like comic sidekicks. They want the films to be tough like Terminator, and they get very upset and opinionated about anything that has anything to do with being childlike.|George Lucas|{{WebCite|url=http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/entertainment/394542.stm|text=Entertainment | Star Wars: Lucas strikes back|date=1999-07-14|work=[[Wikipedia:BBC|BBC]]|archivedate=20090929002301}}}} [[File:JarJarBinksConceptArt-AoEpI.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Concept art of Jar Jar Binks]] Jar Jar Binks was a computer-generated character, voiced by [[Ahmed Best]], who also provided the voice for the games ''[[Star Wars: Super Bombad Racing]]''''[[Star Wars: Super Bombad Racing]]'' and ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''.''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'' Best reprised the role in a first season [[Bombad Jedi|episode]] of ''[[Star Wars: The Clone Wars]]'' TV series, however it was later assigned to [[Phil LaMarr|BJ Hughes]].{{WebCite|url=http://www.theforce.net/topstory/story/ForceCast_In_The_Cantina_with_Dave_Filoni_120494.asp|text=Force-Cast: In The Cantina with Dave Filoni|date=2009-01-21|archivedate=20090126202556}} Best returned to voice the role in the third and fourth seasons with the episodes ''[[Supply Lines]]'',{{SWArchive|url=theclonewars/guide/episode303.html|text=''The Clone Wars'' Episode Guide: Supply Lines}} ''[[Gungan Attack]]'' and ''[[Shadow Warrior]], ''as well as the sixth season's [[The Disappeared, Part I|Disappeared]] story arc. During the filming of the [[prequel trilogy]], Best appeared on set in costume to provide a reference point for the other actors and appeared partially on-screen in a few shots, such as the close-up of Jar Jar's hand getting stuck in Skywalker's podracer. Best also voiced Binks in [[2006]] for ''[[Star Wars]]'' creator [[George Lucas]]'s entry into [[Wikipedia:Stephen Colbert|Stephen Colbert's]] "green screen challenge" for his show [[Wikipedia:The Colbert Report|''The Colbert Report'']],{{SWArchive|url=community/news/media/news20061012.html|text='George L.' Takes Second Place in Colbert's Greenscreen Challenge}}{{SWArchive|url=video/view/0001|text=The Colbert Report: Greenscreen Challenge|nobackup=1}} and as a parody of the character in 2007 for the ''[[Robot Chicken: Star Wars]]'' special.''[[Robot Chicken: Star Wars]]'' The character's name came from [[Jett Lucas]], son of [[George Lucas]].{{HomeVideoCite|film=1|featurette=The Beginning: Making Episode I}} During the early development stages of ''The Phantom Menace'', George Lucas had first envisioned Jar Jar as an "talking, feeling, walking, running, falling, fainting bundle of amphibious comic relief." The [[Gungan/Legends|Gungan]] [[Species/Legends|species]] designs began with Jar Jar Binks, who was one of the most challenging design tasks the Art Department for [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|Episode I]] faced. Once Jar Jar was locked, all the other Gungans were based on him. For crowd shots, [[Industrial Light & Magic]] modified the basic Jar Jar model to come up with thin, fat, short, female and children Gungans to fill out a shot.{{DB|species|gungan|Gungan}} The [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace (video game)|''Star Wars'': Episode I ''The Phantom Menace'' video game]] says that Binks was imprisoned upon his return to Otoh Gunga and Obi-Wan Kenobi rescued him before leaving together for [[Theed/Legends|Theed]]. This plot was invented to give an additional action in the Otoh Gunga mission, but the movie does not show that this event occurred, so this event is non-canon. === Reaction === Many fans pinned their disappointments with [[Star Wars: Episode I The Phantom Menace|''The Phantom Menace'']] on Jar Jar and his comedic antics, which they felt both fell flat on their targets and even offended some viewers.{{WebCite|url=http://adamrulz.com/jj|text=The Jar Jar Hate Page|archivedate=20001206210200}}{{WebCite|url=http://www.chefelf.com/starwars/ep1.php|text=78 Reasons to Hate ''Star Wars Episode I: The Phantom Menace''|archivedate=20041025173508}}{{WebCite|url=http://www.scifimoviepage.com/jarjar.html|text=Jar Jar Binks Must Die|archivedate=20040704045940}} Possibly as a result of fan hostility, Jar Jar's role in [[Star Wars: Episode II Attack of the Clones|''Attack of the Clones'']] made him a pivotal part of the story, as the one who inadvertently helped [[Palpatine/Legends|Palpatine]] lay the foundations of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]], while minimizing his screen time. His role in [[Star Wars: Episode III Revenge of the Sith|''Revenge of the Sith'']] was further reduced to two scenes and only two words. Many Star Wars fans express their distaste for the character of Binks in a variety of media. One such group of disgruntled viewers were prompted to create a fan film named "Jar Jar's Walking Papers," which depicts the death of Jar Jar.{{YouTube|video=--F50TO42zA|text=Jar Jar's Walking Papers|channel=channel/UCYcaX4yNApthWXzrjM0zVQA|name=Donovan Giggles}} [[File:JarJar-Carbonite.jpg|thumb|right|190px|Jar Jar in carbonite, as seen at the Letterman Digital Arts Center]] In "[[Failing Up With Jar Jar Binks]]," Binks being elected after promising "no new taxes" is a reference to American president [[Wikipedia:George H. W. Bush|George H. W. Bush]] and his 1988 election promise of "[[Wikipedia:Read my lips: no new taxes|no new taxes.]]" In the 2008 LucasArts game ''[[Star Wars: The Force Unleashed]]'', while playing on Imperial occupied [[Kashyyyk/Legends|Kashyyyk]], there is a trophy of Jar Jar Binks frozen in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] on the wall of [[Ozzik Sturn]]'s trophy room. It is flanked by mounted trophies of a [[Kowakian monkey-lizard/Legends|Kowakian monkey-lizard]] head and a [[Dianoga/Legends|Dianoga]] eyestalk, both nods to [[Salacious B. Crumb/Legends|Salacious B. Crumb]] and the trash compactor monster from Episode IV. The carbonite-encased Binks is a nod to a full-sized version that a fan made for one of the Star Wars [[Celebration]]s and is now located at the Letterman Digital Arts Center.{{WebCite|url=http://www.empireonline.com/features/insideilm/8.asp|text=Inside ILM|date=2007-12-06|nobackup=1}} ===Possible family=== According to an ambiguously-[[canon]] ''[[Star Wars Tales]]'' [[George R. Binks|comic book story]], Binks's father, [[George R. Binks]], in contrast to his son, was a dignified, intelligent character, who despairs at Binks's foolish antics. [[Jar Jar Binks's mother|His wife]] is assumed to have been the mother of Jar Jar Binks, although George married her because he knew she could bear him an heir, not because he had romantic feelings for her. Also, in the Infinities story [[Tantive IV (comic story)|''Tantive IV'']], [[Abso Bar Binks]] claims to be the son of Binks. ===Jar Jar Binks' fate=== [[File:Jar_Jar_Coruscant.png|thumb|left|250px|Jar Jar, a Quarren, and an IM-6 medical droid in an easter egg in ''Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns'']] The [[Liberation of Coruscant (Galactic Civil War)|Liberation of Coruscant]] mission of the [[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds#Expansion set: Clone Campaigns|''Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns'']] game features a sprite identified as ''Jar Jar'' among the skyscrapers of [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]], seen only if the player decides to explore the whole game map with an air unit or by using cheat codes. This is a superficially canonical indication that Binks was alive and well, and living on Coruscant, during the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] [[New Republic era|era]]. It may also be only an "[[Easter egg]]" like many featured in the game, and thus dubiously canonical. (For example, ''Clone Campaigns'' features sprites of [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] and [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]] appear near a crashed [[Escape pod/Legends|escape pod]] on [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] during a [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]]-era mission.) In the Naboo celebration scene inserted into the end of the 2004-version of [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Return of the Jedi'']], several Gungans are seen taking part in the celebrations. One Gungan can be heard shouting "Wesa free!".{{Film|VI}} ===Speculations of antagonism=== {{Quote|[...] There are people who just didn't like Jar Jar as a character. And that's completely valid. But as far as Jar Jar being a negative creature, no, he wasn't.|Ahmed Best|''[[The Making of Star Wars Revenge of the Sith]]''}} In late October 2015, a Reddit user by the name of "Lumpawarroo" published a theory speculating that Binks was originally written as a major antagonist of the series, as '''Darth Jar Jar''', and a prominent collaborator with Palpatine, before being redacted from the villain's role due to the character's initial (and ongoing) negative reception. The post quickly became viral and received significant media coverage internationally by independent bloggers and major news outlets like ''The Guardian'', ''The Washington Post'', and ''The New York Times'' that included analysis of his actions in ''The Phantom Menace''. Ahmed Best, who portrayed Jar Jar Binks in motion capture and voice, tweeted his thoughts on how it "feels good" when the truth comes out shortly after the theory gained widespread popularity. In 2020 American podcaster and comedian [https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jon_Lovett Jon Lovett] tweeted his story of asking George Lucas about the theory to which the shocked Lucas responded "No. No. Absolutely not."{{Twitter|username=henridefense|url=status/1601794545703739393|name=Boredom Cultivator|archivedate=20230426123316}} ===Non-canon content=== {{Noncanonstart|legends=1}} {{Quote|Dexie, why everybody hate mesa?|Jar Jar Binks|''[[Star Wars Detours]]''}} [[File:LEGO-Gungans.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Jar Jar Binks and Roos Tarpals in ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Video Game]]'']] He was elected to the position of senator on a "no new taxes" platform. During the Clone Wars, Binks was re-elected with wide popular approval, despite the fact that his opponent (another Gungan) brought up his record of clumsiness, political errors, and service in 'war.' His aides tried to convince him to run for [[Supreme Chancellor/Legends|President]], and he may have been contacted by [[Palpatine/Legends|Darth Sidious]]. When contacted by Darth Sidious, he also somehow managed to convince Sidious to work for him.{{Tales|20|Failing Up With Jar Jar Binks}} During his time in the [[Imperial Senate/Legends|Imperial Senate]], "Senator Jar Jar Binks Commemorative Drinking Cups with Flexible Straws and 'Talking Action'" were produced, and were even available on worlds as distant as [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]].{{Tales|20|Melvin Fett (comic story)}} After Binks's retirement, he married and later fathered a son who they named [[Abso Bar Binks]]. He was a kind father and always tried to bring presents home to both his wife and children, but the presents were always confiscated by the Empire at checkpoints. This led his son to join the growing [[Alliance to Restore the Republic/Legends|Rebellion]] and join the crew of the [[Tantive V (CR90 corvette)|''Tantive V'']].{{StoryCite|story=Tantive IV (comic story)|book=Star Wars Manga: Black|stext=''Tantive IV''}} Binks makes a brief appearance in the special ''[[LEGO Star Wars: The Padawan Menace]]'', where he is in the Senate Building during an attack. The result of the attack led to Binks being hit with a blaster bolt and breaking into pieces, though his legs still ran around. Binks can be seen in the Officers' Club on the planet [[Coruscant/Legends|Coruscant]] in the video game [[Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures (video game)|''Star Wars: Clone Wars Adventures'']]. He has his name and the words "[[Gungan Style]]" above him.
